title: Brown hypotheses for admissible coefficients over a geometric finite field
statement: Let D be a finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], let ℓ be prime and distinct from D.p, let aX:X→Spec D.k be a separated finite-type structure morphism, and let Λ be a commutative condensed coefficient ring satisfying the actual six-case admissibility predicate [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Then BrownHypothesesFor Λ X holds, with the full bundle characterized by [lem-sfb-brown-hypotheses-criterion]. In particular, the localizing category has its inherited triangulation and fixed-universe coproducts, its constructible finite-Tor property is thick and essentially small, and every small presentation of that property gives compact generators. The field D.k is the algebraic closure in the datum, not an arbitrary positive-characteristic field.

source.place: paragraphs 1--2: thickness, essential smallness, compact representatives and generation

proof.text: Install the explicit separated finite-type structure morphism as the scheme-over instance. Finite type over the field makes X compact and locally Noetherian.

The structural theorem supplies a coproduct structure on the localizing closure. Apply the existing finite-field objectwise compactness theorem for that structure, keeping D, its characteristic restriction, separated finite type and the actual six-case admissibility predicate explicit. The imported theorem carries out the skeleton choice and compactness transport once.

Use the Noetherian Brown criterion to combine that coproduct-and-objectwise-compactness witness with admissible thickness and smallness. Generation follows from the criterion, so no separate representative choice is elaborated in this assembly.

proof_origin.note: Reuse the proved objectwise finite-field compactness specialization and the Noetherian criterion. This retains every geometric and coefficient hypothesis and moves no hole. Avoid repeating the expensive skeleton assembly in the large Brown module. C2: relocate the unchanged theorem and proof to BrownHypothesesFiniteField, which imports the general criterion module. Its specialized compactness proof no longer belongs to the general criterion module import closure.
